sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome. In this video, we are counting down 35 self-hosted projects on GitHub. Check the description below for links to every repository we mention. Let's get into it.

sections.title: saasmail
paragraphs: Marketing blasts in Mailchimp, billing in Stripe, support, and Zenesk. When a user emails for help, you have zero context on who they are. SAS Mail collapses every interaction into one unified timeline per customer. Marketing, notifications, support. All-in-one self-hosted inbox. 100% native Cloudflare stack. Email workers receive messages. D1 SQLite for the database. R2 for attachments. Native email sending for replies. Practically free. Hister is a personal search

sections.title: hister
paragraphs: engine. Web history on steroids. A background browser extension performs automatic full text indexing of the actual rendered content of every website you visit. Global hotkey pulls up a blazing fast search bar querying your private local index. Beautiful spvelt and go web interface plus a full terminal UI. Readability popup view for reading articles right in search results. Custom aliases for filtering.

sections.title: recipes
paragraphs: Tandoor recipes is a gorgeous self-hosted recipe manager for your home server. Paste any recipe URL and it instantly strips away the blog fluff, extracting pure ingredients, instructions, and photos into a clean database. Drag and drop weekly meal planner, step-by-step cooking mode, one-click serving size scaling, and autogenerated grocery lists grouped by supermarket aisle based on what you planned.

sections.title: bindery
paragraphs: Riadair is essentially dead. The project got archived. The metadata backend went offline. Bindary is the clean room replacement built from scratch and go with a React 19 front end. Solves the metadata nightmare by strictly using stable documented public APIs instead of web scraping. Tell it which authors to monitor. Tracks upcoming releases on a built-in calendar. Organizes your library perfectly.

sections.title: kyoo
paragraphs: Plex and Jellyfin force you to meticulously rename every file and maintains strict folder structures. Q throws that out entirely. Set up once, forget about it. Point it at your messy download directory, and its scanning engine figures everything out, even for anime and TV shows with ridiculously complex file names. Modern multicontainer architecture with isolated distributed transcoding.

sections.title: VaulTLS
paragraphs: Vaults is a self-hosted web app that acts as a centralized certificate authority for your home network. Rust backend, Vue.js front end, modern dashboard for generating and distributing TLS and SSH certificates. OIDC authentication, restful API for automation, automated email notifications beforeerts expire. Deploy in seconds via Docker or Podman.

sections.title: budgetbee
paragraphs: Most personal finance apps either mine your data or lock the good features behind a subscription. BudgetB is the self-hosted alternative. Single Docker container, 100% ownership of your financial data. Clean React and Tailwind front end. Track expenses, set category budgets, monitor upcoming recurring bills. Multicurrency support, multi-user accounts so your whole family can manage separate ledgers on one server.

sections.title: tududi
paragraphs: To duty is a self-hosted task manager built around calm productivity. Clean minimalist hierarchy. Areas contain projects. Projects contain tasks and notes. That's it. Minimalist doesn't mean weak. Smart recurring tasks. Subtasks. Calav sync. Enterprise SSO. Deep Telegram integration. Text your private bot on the go to capture ideas. It organizes them into your 2duty inbox and sends you a daily digest.

sections.title: jcorp-nomad
paragraphs: JCorp Nomad is an offline media server running on a $20 ESP32S3 microcontroller packed into a USB thumb drive form factor. Plug it into any battery bank. It broadcasts its own Wi-Fi hotspot with a captive portal. Anyone nearby connects their phone, tablet, or laptop and instantly streams movies, TV, music, and ebooks directly from the onboard micro SD card. No apps, no internet.

sections.title: OpenVidReview
paragraphs: Frame.io is expensive and locks you into a SAS. Open Vid Review is the self-hosted open-source alternative. Upload videos, share a link, and reviewers add timestamped comments and color-coded tags directly on the player. The killer feature for editors. Export all comments as an EDL file and drop them straight into Da Vinci Resolve or Premiere Pro as markers on your editing timeline.

sections.title: hortusfox-web
paragraphs: Plantare apps are packed with ads or lock features behind subscriptions. Hortis Fox is the free open- source alternative. Self-host it on your home NAS with one docker command. Gorgeous web dashboard to catalog your entire collection. Custom locations for different rooms. Inventory tracking for pots and fertilizers, integrated weather data, built-in plant recognition to identify unknown species.

sections.title: papermerge-core
paragraphs: PaperMerge is a self-hosted document management system for digital archives. Configure your scanner to upload directly. Aperge runs OCR automatically, extracts the data, and injects a fully searchable text overlay onto your PDFs and JPEGs. modern desktop-like web UI with dual panel file browser, drag and drop, hierarchical folders, and custom metadata tagging.

sections.title: trailbase
paragraphs: Firebase alternatives usually mean managing separate microservices for database, O APIs, and real-time updates. Trailbase collapses all of that into a single high-performance executable. Built-in Rust powered by SQLite, submillisecond latencies that eliminate the need for caching layers, autogenerated type-S safe rest APIs, websocket real-time subscriptions, and a full web assembly runtime for custom serverside logic.

sections.title: NetAlertX
paragraphs: Want to know exactly what's connected to your network at all times? Net Alert X is a self-hosted network visibility framework. sits between a basic ping scanner and an expensive enterprise CM tool. Continuously scans your LAN via ARP, DHCP, and SNMP, building a real-time inventory of every connected device. Unknown device joins your Wi-Fi or a trusted device suspiciously changes state. Instant alert.

sections.title: selfsync
paragraphs: Selfsync is a self-hosted Chrome sync server. Spin up a lightweight Docker container. Launch Chrome with the DAS sync URL flag pointing to your local server and your browser syncs everything to your own SQLite database instead of California. No browser extensions needed. Native support for Chromium's Nagori endtoend encryption means your passwords stay encrypted at rest. Even the server can't read them. Nexcloud and Google Drive are bloated if all you need is simple file sharing. Simple Share is

sections.title: simpleShare
paragraphs: built by a group of high school developers from Hungary. Drop and share, zero bloat, Vue3 and Tailwind front end, TypeScript and NodeJS backend powered by Mariab, drag and drop uploads, sharing via unique short codes, user dashboards, group uploads, storage quotas, and a full admin panel.

sections.title: newt
paragraphs: Exposing home lab services usually means opening firewall ports or wrestling with NAT rules. N is a user space wireguard tunnel client and TCP UDP proxy written in Go. It's the edge connector for the Panggalan remote access ecosystem. Drop it behind your home firewall. It automatically reaches out to your Panggalan server, negotiates an encrypted wire guard tunnel over websockets, and securely proxies traffic to specific services on your LAN.

sections.title: panel
paragraphs: Caligopus panel is an ultraast pterodactyl alternative completely rewritten from scratch. Docker as the backbone means you're not limited to Minecraft or Arc. Run any containerized application alongside your games. Connects to a custom Rustbased Wings Damon that's incredibly memory efficient, making it perfect for anything from a Raspberry Pi to a full enterprise rack.

sections.title: borg-ui
paragraphs: Borg backup is incredibly powerful, but managing it through the CLI and SSH is tedious. Borg UI wraps Borg backup in a modern web interface, visual scheduling through a built-in cron builder, live progress tracking when backups are actively running, and easy SSH key management, an archive browser that lets you click through your snapshots like regular folders, and restore specific files with a single click.

sections.title: Octopoda-OS
paragraphs: Octapota OS is an open-source memory operating system for AI agents. Two lines of Python gives your agent persistent long-term memory, semantic search, crash recovery, and built-in loop detection. Everything runs autonomously in the background. Memory survives restarts and deployments. Agents communicate with each other through shared inboxes.

sections.title: SoulSync
paragraphs: Soul Sync is an automated music discovery and collection manager. Bridges mainstream streaming services with your Plex, Jellyfin, or Navadrome server. Connect your Spotify title. It monitors your playlists and followed artists. When a new track drops, it autonomously sources and downloads high-quality files through Soulsek, Daer, or Kobas.

sections.title: BookLore
paragraphs: Booklor is a self-hosted web application that pulls all of it into a stunning centralized library. Drop a file in, it automatically fetches beautiful cover art, author details, and metadata. Built-in reader that seamlessly remembers your scroll position and tracks reading progress across all your devices. Multi-user support, granular sharing permissions.

sections.title: snacks
paragraphs: Massive Plex or jellyfin library running out of disk space. Snacks is an automated video library encoder. Pointed at your folders and it transcodes your massive video files into highly optimized formats using Intel and AMD hardware acceleration in the background. The master coordinator turns them into a unified encoding farm, transferring raw files to idle worker nodes and copying optimized files back when they finish.

sections.title: Maintainerr
paragraphs: Tired of playing janitor for your Plex or jellyfin server? Your friends use Overseer to request dozens of movies? Then those files just sit there unwatched for months eating your hard drive. Maintainer looks like Seir, but does the opposite. An automated library maintenance tool that integrates with radar, sonar, and tuli. Set custom rules to hunt down unwatched or outdated media.

sections.title: qlib
paragraphs: QIB is a quantitative investment platform with an end-to-end machine learning pipeline built specifically for finance. Blazing fast data processing, automated feature engineering, highly optimized trading simulation engine. comes preloaded with state-of-the-art models like GBM to complex deep learning architectures ready to forecast stock movements out of the box.

sections.title: Lidify
paragraphs: Litify is a personalized recommendation engine for your local music library. Connects to your LAR instance, scans the artists you already love, and uses the last FM API to figure out exactly what bands you should be listening to next. Run it via Docker, configure with your LiDAR quality profiles, and it automatically searches for missing albums the second it adds a new artist.

sections.title: note-mark
paragraphs: Notion is bloated and slow to load. Notemark is the self-hosted alternative. Sleek, lightning fast web-based markdown notes app, responsive UI, built-in dark and light themes, WASOM powered markdown renderer. The best part is the back end. Instead of a complex proprietary database, Notemark uses a custom flat file storage system. Your notes are just readable text files on disk.

sections.title: reisenotiz
paragraphs: Rise notets is an offline first progressive web app for managing your trips. Self-hosted dashboard that tracks flights, hotels, and passenger details in one gorgeous timeline view. Automatic airport lookups via IAT codes. Complex time zone math handled for you. Because it's offline first, you install it on your phone and check your itinerary mid-flight with zero internet connection.

sections.title: noton
paragraphs: You want a massive internal knowledge base, but refuse to upload company docs to the cloud. Noton is a self-hosted documentation platform built on Laravel and Filament. Beautifully structured interface focused on clarity out-of-the-box integration with Olama and OpenClaw for completely local private AI features. Users ask contextual questions through a built-in chat that summarizes answers based strictly on your private docs.

sections.title: tinyfeed
paragraphs: Heavy-bloated RSS readers are overkill when all you want is a newsboard. Tiny Feed is a minimalist CLI tool written in Go. Zero dependencies. Feed it a list of RSS, Atom, or JSON URLs, and it generates a blazing fast static HTML page aggregating everything. No database, no complex configs. Run it via cron or use the built-in demon mode to continuously update your page. PAH is a highly specialized self-hosted reverse geocoding service originally built to

sections.title: paikka
paragraphs: power the rayy location tracker written in Java ingests raw Open Street Map PBF data and spins up a blazing fast offline resolution engine right inside a Docker container. Feed it coordinates. It instantly returns the exact place, city, and street name. process millions of location points locally, securely, zero API cost.

sections.title: squarebox
paragraphs: Connecting AI agents to your local machine usually feels like a security risk. Squarebox is a high performance MCP server built for local first automation. It lets your AI like Claude securely interact with your file system, run terminal commands, and manage local processes with zero latency. Your agent gets the hands it needs to be a real developer assistant. Your data stays strictly on your machine.

sections.title: trackarr
paragraphs: If you're on multiple private trackers, you know the pain. Log into each one. Eyeball your ratio. Hope you're not about to get flagged for hidden runs. Trackar pulls it all into one dashboard. Register integrations. Schedule syncs with chron expressions. Store historical snapshots. Get per tracker cards showing ratio. Upload and download totals. Seed bonus and buffer with visual warnings when you drop below minimum.

sections.title: familiar
paragraphs: Every music player searches by artist, album, or genre. Familiar searches by sound. Type something melancholy with piano or acoustic and upbeat, and it queries the audio itself. No tags required. Every track in your library gets a clap embedding, the Lion model trained on millions of audio text pairs. Claude is built in with 25 tools. Semantic search, band camp, purchase recommendations.

sections.title: modelship
paragraphs: Running multiple AI models locally means juggling five Docker containers, weird port configs, and constant resource fights. Models ship packs everything into a single unified inference server. One clean, OpenAI compatible API for your entire AI stack. Define what you want in a simple models.yaml. Allocate GPU or CPU resources. Pick loaders like VLM transformers or diffusers.
